direct_file_reviews.summary: Reverse-engineering prompt requiring an original executable-compatible CLI implementation from bundled docs and observed binary behavior only.
Parallel codex metadata shows actual parallel use, four subagents, finished state, and stale quality fields of 529/1085.
Current completed official evaluation supersedes aggregates and records a failed parallel solution with 529 passed and 555 failed cases.
Official evaluator summary confirms broad but incomplete ProgramBench coverage for the parallel delivered artifact.
Final response states the active package-based reimplementation and acknowledges approximate multi-file 7z metadata.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport wrapper for the parallel run; it contains no projected semantic events but accounts for the top-level cell transcript.
Parent trajectory spawns doc and probe children, performs its own checks, observes the executable selecting another path, adopts the package implementation, cleans the workspace, and finalizes.
Child trajectory probes behavior and builds the package-based implementation with reimpl.py, src/sevenza/app.py, src/sevenza/libarchive7z.py, and a compile script.
CLI probe child records command, archive, stream, mutation, hash, and error-behavior observations used by the rest of the parallel run.
Concurrent implementation trajectory writes a monolithic main.py plus compile.sh, detects that the active executable has been changed to reimpl.py, reconciles, deletes main.py, and finalizes.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Same reverse-engineering prompt requiring a clean-room implementation from bundled docs and behavioral observation.
Serial codex metadata shows no parallel use, no subagents, finished state, and quality fields of 615/1085.
Current completed official evaluation records a failed serial solution with 615 passed and 469 failed cases.
Official evaluator summary confirms the serial artifact failed but covered more cases than parallel.
Final response states a standalone src/sevenzip_compat.py implementation, compile.sh installation, verified parity cases, and remaining backend risks.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport wrapper for the serial run; it contains no projected semantic events and records the single-agent cell transcript.
Single serial agent probes the CLI, implements one src/sevenzip_compat.py file, wires compile.sh, runs side-by-side parity tests, and finalizes with known remaining 7z and bzip2 backend risks.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the need for a clean-room 7-Zip-like executable based on bundled docs and normal CLI probing, with no source-code lookup or runtime delegation to the original binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It split early into doc and CLI probing children, but implementation ownership became overlapping: separate live actors produced package, monolithic, and launcher-oriented paths that all claimed the final executable surface.
parallel.implementation: The delivered path became reimpl.py plus src/sevenza/app.py and src/sevenza/libarchive7z.py, covering help, errors, archive operations, streams, hashing, and several formats through Python and libarchive.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration was disturbed when the active ./executable was changed to dispatch to reimpl.py while another path was testing main.py; the parent then adopted the package path, deleted main.py, and rebuilt the launcher.
parallel.verification: The final checks covered help, bad switch/command errors, archive create/list/test/extract, stdin/stdout, no-input behavior, zip auto-extension, warning exits, and overwrite quit behavior.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run acknowledged approximate multi-file 7z internal listing metadata, especially header size, packed-size display, and block accounting, and the official evaluation failed 529/1085.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room constraints and built against observed CLI behavior and bundled documentation without subagents or external source lookup.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, build wiring, and final verification in a single path, avoiding cross-agent entrypoint or source ownership ambiguity.
serial.implementation: It implemented src/sevenzip_compat.py and a compile.sh that installed that source as ./executable, covering CLI surface, archive list/test/extract, hashing, create/update/delete/rename, and stream behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The build path remained coherent: compile.sh installed the single implementation file as the executable and subsequent checks exercised that same delivered path.
serial.verification: The serial run compared exact output against the preserved original for help, info, unsupported commands, original archive listing/testing/extraction, stream extraction, hashing, multiple creation paths, and a tar stdin error.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: It still failed the official evaluation at 615/1085, with stated residual risk in exact 7z create/update parity and bzip2 creation backend behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel understood that the required deliverable was an original executable-compatible CLI based on observed behavior and bundled documentation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt constraints and targeted the same 7-Zip command surface without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the central requirements; the difference is not a prompt misunderstanding but how each translated them into a stable implementation and verification path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across doc reading, CLI probing, and multiple implementation actors, then allowed overlapping ownership of the final build and executable path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership in one trajectory and produced one implementation file plus one compile script.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained breadth from children but had to reconcile ownership; serial avoided handoff and ownership conflicts at the cost of doing all work sequentially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not maintain a stable cross-agent contract for which source tree and compile script owned the submitted executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent interface; the compile script directly installed the same implementation file it had been testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's active entrypoint became ambiguous and had to be re-inspected, while serial kept file, launcher, and tests aligned.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ultimately shipped reimpl.py with a src/sevenza package and a libarchive-backed 7z layer, while acknowledging approximate multi-file 7z metadata.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial shipped src/sevenzip_compat.py and reported broader command coverage with remaining risks in 7z create/update and bzip2 creation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's single implementation path reached higher evaluated coverage; parallel's package path was functional but inherited less time for final precision after reconciliation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received child results and did eventually adopt the package result, but only after discovering the active build no longer matched another in-progress implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and moved directly from local implementation to local verification and finalization.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel result lifecycle included late reconciliation of a child-produced implementation and launcher; serial's local result never needed cross-agent retrieval or adoption.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had shared-workspace integration trouble: competing compile scripts and entrypoints changed the active executable during testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one compile script to install one source file as ./executable and kept subsequent verification on that path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-state collision around the submitted artifact; serial did not expose shared write state because there was only one writer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reran representative checks through the final executable and disclosed the remaining 7z metadata approximation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified a broader exact-parity matrix against the preserved original before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both failed official evaluation, but serial's verification was more coherent and correlates with its higher pass count.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without timeout but used four subagents, many more tool calls, and had to spend closure effort cleaning and reconciling shared state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished without timeout and used one trajectory with fewer tool calls and no parallel-control overhead.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's fan-out did not time out, but the reconciliation work reduced useful closure time; serial spent its budget directly on one implementation and verification path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both runs failed the completed evaluator. The material difference is coverage, with serial passing 615/1085 and parallel passing 529/1085. The serial run kept one implementation and build path, while the parallel run had a deliverable entrypoint overwritten between competing implementations and then spent integration time reconciling and deleting the abandoned path. That coordination episode is a supported adverse contributor to lower parallel coverage, not a proven exclusive root cause of the failed outcome.
parallel_contributors: Concurrent deliverable overwrite changed the active executable away from the main.py path during verification.
Final parallel delivery still acknowledged approximate multi-file 7z metadata.
serial_contributors: Single implementation path kept source, compile script, and executable aligned.
Serial final verification covered a broader exact-parity matrix before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations remained imperfect archive backends rather than exact 7-Zip replicas.
Parallel's known gap centered on 7z listing metadata; serial's known gap centered on 7z create/update and bzip2 create parity.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation was actively owned by multiple agents; the problem was overlapping ownership, not absence of an implementation owner.
The parent explicitly inspected and reconciled the active package path, so integration was not unowned.
Multiple agents assembled launchers and compile scripts; the failure was conflicting assembly ownership, not missing assembly ownership.
The parent retained end-to-end responsibility for build, test, cleanup, and final delivery after child work returned.
The run did not block all productive work behind one mandatory serial preflight; children and parent probed and implemented concurrently.
Investigation and implementation overlapped rather than forming a separate investigation-only phase that delayed all productive work.
The critical implementation path was active in several agents; the observed harm is the write collision, not lack of implementation capacity.
Although fan-out increased tool and token use, the run finished and the concrete adverse event was executable ownership collision, not collective exhaustion before closure.
No single child received a uniquely overbroad task whose incomplete return drove the result; multiple actors completed usable but conflicting implementations.
The children knew the broad clean-room CLI task and produced relevant work; no already-known task or acceptance requirement is shown missing from a child brief and causing unusable work.
There was no separate component-interface contract failure; the same episode is better classified as a concrete deliverable overwrite of the active launcher.
No specific known finding disappeared through summary or transfer and caused repeated work or an incorrect action.
Returned child information was long but was inspected and used; the adverse effect came from conflicting workspace state, not unconsumed bulk.
The active state changed, but the agents observed the changed executable and compile path rather than relying on a stale returned report.
There were competing codepaths, but the decisive evidence is a file-level launcher overwrite, not incompatible reports left unadjudicated.
Parallel did perform integrated final checks and explicitly disclosed a remaining 7z metadata gap; no parent-only unsupported completion decision is evidenced apart from evaluator failure.
No replacement or retry agent is shown repeating prior work because it lacked inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No needed child was explicitly cancelled or interrupted before a required result was available.
The final package implementation was built and delivered; there is no complete separate candidate that simply missed promotion before closure.
After adopting the package path, the parent ran additional checks through the active compile.sh/executable, so the result was not merely merged after verification with no recheck.
The child package implementation was retrieved and joined into final delivery; the issue was how it displaced another active implementation.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that remained trapped below the parent before closure.
No required child failure or cancellation was left without takeover; the parent took over integration and final cleanup.
Completed child implementation results were inspected, adopted, or superseded explicitly rather than silently ignored.
The parent did not wait blindly to a timeout; it inspected workspace state and child results and the run finished without timeout.
The competing implementation paths are real, but the same chain includes a more specific active executable replacement, so the broader cross-file label is suppressed by taxonomy precedence.
Both paths touched compile.sh, but the observed consequence was the required executable changing owners; deliverable overwrite is the higher-precedence label for this chain.
The deleted main.py was an alternate entrypoint cleanup after adopting the other path, not an independent overwrite of a non-entry library or module.

Concurrent agents produced competing final launchers: one path added main.py and compile.sh, another added a compile.sh that generated ./executable for reimpl.py, and the active implementer observed that ./executable had changed away from the path under test.
candidates.realized_consequence: Tests against the main.py path stopped representing the submitted executable, forcing a mid-run switch to the package implementation, deletion of the alternate entrypoint, and reduced final polish before a lower-scoring failed delivery.
candidates.near_match_reason: The source-tree collision was present, but the required executable was the actual overwritten deliverable, which is more specific and has precedence.

candidates.reason: Cleanup removed many temporary outputs but kept the adopted implementation; there was no broad promotion replacing another complete final tree beyond the executable chain.
The workspace was shared, but the specific observed problem is the executable/launcher overwrite, so the generic unisolated-write label is not retained.
Temporary archives and probe outputs accumulated, but no actor is shown consuming another actor's generated artifact as a reference environment in a way that contaminated behavior.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel run had concurrent final-artifact ownership. The monolithic path wrote main.py and a compile script, while the package path wrote a compile script that generated ./executable for reimpl.py. The active implementer later observed that ./executable had changed away from main.py during testing and had to reconcile and delete the displaced entrypoint.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The main.py path's verification became unreliable because ./executable no longer ran that code, leading to explicit inspection of the divergence, adoption of the package path, deletion of main.py, and less final refinement than the serial run.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The files also represented competing source scopes, but the observed replacement of the submitted executable is more specific and higher precedence.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Cross-File Scope Collision, Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, and Unisolated Workspace Writes describe the same launcher/codepath conflict at lower specificity or lower precedence.
Load imbalance and merge-after-verification symptoms were downstream of the deliverable overwrite rather than separate allocation or lifecycle episodes.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no separate context, lifecycle, retry, ownership, or contamination episode clears the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained label is limited to one concrete deliverable-overwrite episode with distinct anchors, consequence, serial contrast, and corrective boundary.
